newsitem.title: USA: Delmarva says Salem outages hurt '96 earns.
newsitem.headline: Delmarva says Salem outages hurt '96 earns.

text.p: Delmarva Power & Light Co said Thursday that continuing outages at the Salem Nuclear Generating Station in Salem County, N.J., decreased earnings by about $0.19 a share in 1996.
Delmarva had just reported 1996 earnings of $1.77 a share, off $0.02 from 1995 and fourth quarter 1966 earnings of $0.33 a share, up from $0.29 a share in the comparable 1995 quarter.
"Despite the negative financial impact of Salem, 1996 was a year of substantial achievement," said Howard Cosgrove, Delmarva's chairman, president and chief executive officer.
Excluding costs associated with Salem, earnings rose $0.08 per shares in 1996, primarily due to additional revenues from customer growth, he said.
But the increased revenues were partly offset by higher depreciation expenses, he said.

Delmarva owns a stake of 7.41 percent in the Salem facility. The other owners are Public Service Electric Gas & Co., a unit of Public Service Enterprise Group Inc, and PECO Energy Co, which each own a 42.59 percent stake. Another 7.41 percent stake is held by Atlantic Energy Inc.
